items.performers: Gidon Kremer and Tatjana Grindenko (violins); Alfred Schnittke (prepared piano); Lithuanian Chamber Orchestra; Saulius Sondeckis (conductor)
items.label: ECM New Series
items.note: Two solo violins lead this double concerto through eight variations before the slow “Silentium”, in which the voices move at different speeds. Kremer and Grindenko, the violin soloists at the première, are joined by Alfred Schnittke on prepared piano on the album that launched ECM’s New Series, released in 1984. It is the recording to start with, and Kremer and Keith Jarrett’s Fratres opens the same album.

items.work: Spiegel im Spiegel — violin and piano
items.label: ECM New Series
items.note: The violin’s phrases lengthen above three-note piano arpeggios, returning each time to A. Spivakov, the work’s dedicatee, and Bezrodny open the album Alina with this version, recorded in Frankfurt’s Festeburgkirche with Pärt and Manfred Eicher present. The 1999 album has two works, with Alexander Malter’s long performances of Für Alina between three accounts of Spiegel im Spiegel; Malter and Dietmar Schwalke are the other players.

items.work: Passio Domini nostri Jesu Christi secundum Joannem
items.performers: The Hilliard Ensemble; Michael George (bass); John Potter (tenor); Christopher Bowers-Broadbent (organ); The Western Wind Chamber Choir; Paul Hillier (conductor)
items.label: ECM New Series
items.note: Four singers share the Evangelist’s words in Pärt’s Latin St John Passion, and an organ accompanies Jesus and Pilate. The Hilliard Ensemble’s recording with Paul Hillier, made in St Jude’s on the Hill in London, is an essential account of the long Passion. The Hilliards sing steadily with very little vibrato, so each interval is clear; the recording brought the work to international attention and convinced Pärt, after years of doubt, that the score worked.
